meta.title: Gocci — Keep Google Drive on an external disk, in Finder
meta.description: Downloads land on the disk you choose. Opening a folder pulls nothing down. A small macOS menu bar app.

hero.title:
Drive in Finder.
Files on your own disk.
hero.tagline: What you download goes to the disk you picked. Opening a folder downloads nothing at all.
hero.note: Free and open source. The first launch shows an "unidentified developer" warning

problem.title: Why this exists
problem.lead: The startup disk was full, so Google Drive had to live on an external one. No existing tool would do it.

items.title: Google's own app
items.body: No say in where files are kept. It fills the startup disk, which had 42GB free.

items.title: Mountain Duck
items.body: On macOS the docs say it always lands in ~/Library/CloudStorage. Your chosen path is ignored.

items.title: CloudMounter
items.body: It can use an external disk, but it costs money and shows every file you ever opened via a share link.

items.title: Keeps files on your disk
items.body: Downloads go to the disk you pick in Settings. Your startup disk stays as free as it was. It shows up as GoogleDrive at the top of that disk.

items.title: Opening a folder downloads nothing
items.body: macOS is told the contents live in the cloud, so Finder just lists names. A folder full of video opens instantly.

items.title: Thumbnails still appear
items.body: There is a separate channel for artwork, so drawing an icon never pulls the file down.

items.title: Only the part you read
items.body: Skip into the middle of a large file and only that part is fetched. Jumping into a 70GB video does not fetch 70GB.

items.title: No shared items in the way
items.body: Files you opened through a share link never show up. You see what your browser's My Drive shows.

items.title: Managed the way macOS does it
items.body: Finder marks what is downloaded. Right-click offers Remove Download, and Settings can clear the lot.

screens.title: Screens
screens.lead: All that stays on screen is the menu bar mark. Settings fit on one page.
screens.menu: The menu: whether it is connected, and how to open or disconnect it
screens.settings: Settings: where files are kept, credentials, clearing downloads

how.title: How it works
how.body: Gocci registers with macOS as a File Provider — the same mechanism iCloud Drive uses, so the system knows the contents live in the cloud. rclone handles talking to Drive, and nothing is mounted.
points: Writing works normally. Copy, delete and rename from Finder
Files added on another machine show up within a minute
rclone ships inside the app, pinned to a version that was tested

steps.title: Install it
steps.body: Download the DMG and drag Gocci into Applications. The first launch is blocked, so allow it from System Settings → Privacy & Security.

steps.title: Connect Drive
steps.body: Run rclone config to create one drive remote, and make your own client ID while you are there. The README walks through it.

steps.title: Pick a disk
steps.body: Open Settings and choose your external disk under Stored on. From then on it connects at every login.
